To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) maximum likelihood is the best way to estimate the probability of truth for a given observation, (2) the maximum likelihood solution for conflicting observations outperforms our previous maximum likelihood solution for corroborating observations and the state-of-the art fact-finding algorithms, and (3) maximum likelihood outperforms simple heuristics like majority voting.

(i) the maximum likelihood approach to the truth discovery problem for social sensing is superior to all the baselines, and (ii) the maximum likelihood solution for corroborating and conflicting observations is superior to the maximum likelihood solution when considering corroborating observations alone.

(1) we provide the first maximum likelihood approach to truth discovery for conflicting observations; (2) our approach is shown to be superior to the state-of-the art fact-finding baselins as well as simple voting heuristics; (3) we show that our previous work for corroborating observations can be improved; and (4) the proposed approach is shown to scale to large data sets.
